Topic: More posts won't fix an unclear offer.
Audience problem: The owner keeps posting but cannot explain the offer in one sentence.
Objective: Teach a small message fix and establish the studio's useful, direct tone.
Hook / first frame: Before you write another post, finish this sentence.
Script / slide copy: Before you write another post, finish this sentence: I help a specific customer get a useful result with what I actually sell. Here is an example: I help busy homeowners book a reliable cleaner for their apartment. Now check your bio and your latest post. Do they both make that offer clear? If not, fix the sentence before you make more content. Clarity first. Volume second.
Shot order / edit:
0–3s: face + “Finish this sentence.”
3–13s: show the three-part sentence; label it EXAMPLE.
13–25s: cut to a simple bio mock-up, also labelled EXAMPLE.
25–34s: return to face; “Clarity first. Volume second.”
Chest-up approved owner avatar, eye-level, plain warm background. Insert a three-line message worksheet. No fake office, microphone or client screenshots.
Target 30–38 seconds after recording. Keep the first frame on the face. Use one worksheet cutaway and one gentle reframe. Correct captions and keep the AI-presenter label visible.

Topic: A price is not the end of the reply.
Audience problem: The seller sends a number and the chat goes quiet.
Objective: Give a usable reply structure without promising a sale.
Hook / first frame: If you sell on WhatsApp, don't send the price alone.
Script / slide copy: If you sell on WhatsApp, don't send the price alone. Give three things: the price, what it includes, and one sensible next question. For example: the bag is twenty thousand naira, delivery is separate, and it comes in black or brown. Which colour would you like? That's an example, so use your real price and terms. You're making the next step clear, not pressuring someone to buy.

3–12s: three lines: price / scope / next question.

Caption:
Price + what it includes + one useful next question. Adapt the example to your actual price, delivery terms and product. This can make a reply clearer; it cannot guarantee a sale. Save the structure for your next enquiry.

Topic: Why our portfolio says sample.
Audience problem: Prospects cannot tell sample work from real client engagements.
Objective: Build trust by explaining the evidence honestly.
Hook / first frame: Every project in our portfolio has a label: sample.

Ask why we made each choice. And if someone shows you a result, ask what evidence sits behind it.
